subject: Architecture
title: Circular Architecture: No More Waste
description: A fast breakdown of Circular Architecture: No More Waste for builders.

hook.text: In a circular economy, nothing is waste — every building component is designed for its next life.

buildup.text: Bolted steel connections replace welds so beams can be unbolted and reused in new buildings.

discovery.text: Material passports track every component — what it's made of, where it came from, and where it can go next.

twist.text: The Netherlands built a fully circular office — every piece can be returned, recycled, or composted.

climax.text: By 2050, the EU aims to make all construction circular — buildings as banks of reusable resources.

punchline.text: Demolition is a design failure. The future takes buildings apart, not down.

quiz.question: What is a 'material passport' in circular architecture?
options: A license required to import building materials
A record tracking each component's composition and future reuse potential
A certificate proving materials meet safety standards
